headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: Open Interpreter can modify the user machine while the paired content-writing repo offers no isolation or runtime controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repo with no runnable agent or I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B's outputs by default. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste into Open Interpreter, which is a low-risk prompt-injection path. Because A has no execution surface and B's clipboard/files are user-mediated, the pairwise pathway is limited.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies A-generated text into B's prompt or clipboard, injection becomes possible.
IF B is run with --auto_run, copied instructions can be executed with less friction.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workflows; do not paste A outputs into B without review.
Disable clipboard-based transfer between the two tools.
Run B without --auto_run.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from pasted content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress, while A is a docs-only repository with no runtime isolation or data-handling controls. If A's content is copied into B or B is pointed at files related to A, B can exfiltrate local data to model providers or other endpoints. The interaction is inferred from B's documented surfaces; A provides no containment.
conditions: IF B is given access to directories containing sensitive files, those files can be read and transmitted.
IF the operator pastes A-derived content containing secrets into B, B may forward it to configured model providers.
mitigations: Restrict B to a dedicated empty workspace.
Remove secrets from any directory B can read.
Use local-only model providers for B where possible.
Review and redact pasted content before sending it to B.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and per-process shared state via filesystem, so concurrent instances can collide on the same mutable resources. A is a content-writing repo with no locking or runtime coordination fields, so there is no evidence of conflict prevention. Uncertainty about A's runtime behavior does not reduce the risk; the documented overlap is enough to treat shared writes as dangerous.
conditions: IF two B instances target the same directory, file and git state races can occur.
IF A-generated artifacts are stored in the same workspace B edits, B can overwrite them without coordination.
mitigations: Assign each B instance a separate working directory.
Avoid concurrent git operations on the same repo.
Use filesystem locks or a single-writer policy.
Snapshot the workspace before running B.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can supply content that B may treat as source material, and B's tool-use pattern allows acting on generated code blocks after confirmation. There is no documented verification layer between them, so A's output can cascade into B's actions or edits. A is not an execution agent, but B's authority makes the downstream error path real.
conditions: IF A's text is copied into B as instructions or code, B may execute or write based on it.
IF B is run in auto-run mode, the verification barrier is reduced.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before feeding them to B.
Keep B out of auto-run mode.
Ask B to summarize and verify A's claims before acting.
Limit B to non-destructive commands during the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: A is a public open-source repository with no data classes touched, while B can access anything reachable on the local machine and may handle model-provider API keys. The pair does not show a specific residency or regulated-data mismatch, but B's broad local access creates a compliance gap if regulated files are present. A is not cited for data residency because it does not process such data.
conditions: IF regulated data is present on the local machine and B can read that directory, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF model-provider API keys are stored in files B can access, retention and logging policies become relevant.
mitigations: Exclude regulated directories from B's workspace.
Store secrets outside B-readable paths.
Document which data classes B may touch.
Use a separate machine for regulated workloads.
